**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 29</mark>**<sup>**th**</sup> **<mark>April 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for January 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for January 2011 world copper supply and demand in its April 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for January 2011 showed a deficit of 20,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, January showed a larger deficit of 48,000 t. This compares with a production surplus of 86,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 67,000 t) in January of 2010. 

In January 2011, world usage is estimated to have increased by 11% (158,000 t) compared with that in January 2010. Chinese apparent usage<sup>*****</sup> grew by 12%, but when compared with that in December 2010, it decreased by 5%.  Other contributors to higher consumption in January 2011 were the EU and the United Sates, where aggregated usage grew by 7.5%. 

World mine production grew by 3.7% (48,000 t) in January 2011 compared with that in January 2010: Concentrate production grew by 4.3% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) was up by 1.6%. In part, this relative increase reflects operational constraints that reduced production in January 2010 in Australia, Chile and Mexico. Compared to average monthly production in the 4<sup>th</sup> quarter 2010, mine production in January was down by 6%. This is reflected in the capacity utilization rate that fell to around 78% in January from 84% in 4<sup>th</sup> quarter 2010. On a regional basis, production in January rose by 6.9% in Africa, 3.9% in the Americas, 6.7% in Europe, and 25.7% in Oceania, and declined by 5.8% in Asia. 

In January 2011, world refined production increased by 3.3% (51,000 t) compared with that in the same month of 2010: Primary production increased by 3.5%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 2.3%. Growth in Australia (recovery from low January 2010 level), China and Africa more than offset declines in Chile, the United Sates, Canada and Japan.  On a regional basis, refined production increased by 32% in Africa, 3.7% in Asia, 4.2% in Europe and, 73% in Oceania, but decreased in the Americas by 5.7%. Refined production capacity utilization in January 2011 was around the same level as in January 2010 (78%) but lower than in the 4<sup>th</sup> quarter 2010 (79.6%). 

The average LME cash price for March 2011 was US$9,530.65 per tonne, down from the February 2011 average of US$9,867.58 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of March were US$10,148 and US$9,330 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$9,645.56 per tonne. As of the end of March 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 687,933 t, an increase of 119,751 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010. Compared

to the February levels, stocks were up at the three Exchanges.
